title: Finite normalization of smooth Deligne--Mumford stacks and its charts
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal X$ be a smooth finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over $k$. Let $U\subseteq\mathcal X$ be a dense open substack and let $V\to U$ be a representable finite etale morphism. The meanings of stack, Deligne--Mumford stack and 2-fibre product are those spelled out in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. On each normal finite-type etale scheme chart $T\to\mathcal X$, take the integral closure of $\mathcal O_T$ in the product of the function fields of all generic components of $V\times_{\mathcal X}T$. These finite $T$-schemes and their descent arrows define a normal Deligne--Mumford stack $\mathcal N$ with a representable finite morphism $\nu:\mathcal N\to\mathcal X$. Formation of $\mathcal N$ commutes with etale scheme charts, and there is a canonical equivalence $\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal X}U\simeq V$ over $U$.

If $k$ is perfect (every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable), formation of this normalization also commutes with extension of scalars to every field $k′/k$, using all generic components after base change. There is also the following formal-chart compatibility, under the additional hypothesis that $k$ is perfect. Let $x$ be a geometric point over an algebraically closed field $\Omega/k$, and suppose the formal completion of $\mathcal X_\Omega$ along the residual gerbe of $x$ is presented as $[\operatorname{Spf}R/H]$, with an effective morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\mathcal X_\Omega$ inducing this formal chart, where $R$ is a complete regular Noetherian local $\Omega$-algebra with residue field $\Omega$ and $H=\operatorname{Aut}(x)$ is a finite group. A residual gerbe here means the full substack of objects locally isomorphic to $x$; a quotient by $H$ means the groupoid of $H$-torsors with equivariant maps to the indicated formal scheme. Let $R^\circ\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ be the inverse image of $U_\Omega$, let $E=V_\Omega\times_{U_\Omega}R^\circ$, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $R$ in the product of the generic fields of $E$. The completion of $\mathcal N_\Omega$ along its fibre over that gerbe is $[\operatorname{Spf}B/H]$. In particular the automorphism group of a geometric point above $x$, represented by a closed point $b$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, is the stabilizer $\{h\in H:h(b)=b\}$. Fields, schemes, finite type, finite morphisms, etaleness and smoothness (of an etale scheme atlas over $k$) use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

This stack/formal extension is agent-formulated from those arguments. Perfect-field scalar extension: Tag 038O in varieties.tex (lemma-geometrically-normal), equivalence with normality over the perfect closure; finite birational normal models give the normalization identification.

proof.text: Choose finite-type etale scheme charts $T\to\mathcal X$. They are smooth over $k$, so their stalks are normal. The normal Noetherian scheme $T$ is a finite disjoint union of normal integral components. Work on one such component. Its inverse image $T^\circ$ of $U$ is dense, since the etale chart is flat and open; the same follows from scheme-theoretic density and flat pullback. The finite etale scheme $P=V\times_U T^\circ$ is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes. Pull back the schematically dense map $\operatorname{Spec}k(T)\to T^\circ$ along the flat map $P\to T^\circ$: its image is schematically dense in $P$. The generic fibre algebra is a finite product of finite separable extensions of $k(T)$ by the etale-algebra-over-field theorem. Each open integral component meets this dense fibre, whose points are generic there. Thus the fields in the item are exactly these factors.

source.place: Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); normal components and flat density as in the cited nodes.

proof.text: For an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$, let $L$ be the product of the rational fields of the components of $P|_W$ and let $C\subset L$ be the integral closure of $A$. An element of $L$ integral over $A$ belongs to every local ring of $P|_W$, because those rings are normal and the same monic equation has coefficients in each of them. It is therefore a regular global function on $P|_W$. Consequently $C$ is also the integral closure of $A$ in $\Gamma(P|_W,\mathcal O)$, which is finite over $A$ by the cited finite-etale-open lemma. Its prime localizations are normal by the integral-closure-in-a-product lemma. Localization compatibility glues these affine schemes to a finite normal $N_T\to T$. Each nonempty factor has the prescribed rational field by the integral-closure fraction-field lemma, so $P$ will be dense in $N_T$.

source.place: Tags 032L, 0307 and 035L, as instantiated in the cited statements; construction on normal chart components.

proof.text: Over an affine open $W\subset T^\circ$, the finite etale algebra $D$ of $P|_W$ is normal and finite over $A=\mathcal O_T(W)$. Every element of $D$ is integral over $A$. Conversely, an element of its total rational algebra integral over $A$ is integral over $D$, hence belongs to $D$ by normality. Thus $C=D$ on these opens. These equalities give a canonical isomorphism $N_T|_{T^\circ}\simeq P$, including the empty-cover case. The generic-field construction and normality also show that this open is schematically dense in $N_T$.

For an affine etale change $A\to A'$ of integral chart opens, use the etale integral-closure theorem with ambient algebra $L$, the product of generic fields from step 1. The generic algebra $A'\otimes_A k(T)$ is a product of finite separable fields by the etale-algebra-over-field theorem. The normal-domain-factor theorem for $A'$ and flat density identify these factors with its total rational fields; applying the same field theorem after adjoining the factors of $L$ identifies $A'\otimes_A L$ with the total rational algebra of the pulled-back open cover. Thus the base-change isomorphism for integral closures identifies $A'\otimes_A C$ with the required new normalization algebra. For general chart maps work on these affine opens and glue. On algebraic-space overlaps use etale scheme covers. All comparisons are the canonical maps in these rational algebras, so their triple-overlap composites agree. Effective descent of finite schemes gives $\nu:\mathcal N\to\mathcal X$ representable finite, with precisely $N_T$ as atlas pullbacks; its normal atlas makes $\mathcal N$ normal and Deligne--Mumford. Full faithfulness descends step 3 to $\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal X}U\simeq V$ and proves independence of the atlas.

Suppose $k$ is perfect and $k'/k$ is arbitrary. On an affine normal chart model $\operatorname{Spec}C=N_T$, the perfect-closure criterion applied with perfect closure $k$ itself shows that $C\otimes_k k'$ is normal. It is finite over the base-changed chart algebra, and its open restriction is $P_{k'}$. The open remains schematically dense by flat pullback. On each normal component the total rational algebra is consequently the product of the rational fields of $P_{k'}$, including any splitting of the original generic fields. A finite normal algebra $D$ with this total rational algebra is its integral closure over the base algebra: one inclusion is finiteness, and the reverse inclusion follows because a monic equation over the base is also monic over $D$. Thus the base-changed model is precisely the newly constructed normalization. These identifications are canonical algebra inclusions; they commute with the descent arrows of step 4 and give the asserted scalar-extension equivalence.

source.place: Tag 038O (lemma-geometrically-normal), normality over the perfect closure; affine identification by integral closure.

proof.text: Apply step 5 with $k'=\Omega$. For the specified effective formal chart, the completed-atlas comparison supplies an etale scheme chart $(T,t)$ over $\mathcal X_\Omega$ with $R\simeq\widehat A$, where $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, compatible with the actual map to $\mathcal X_\Omega$. Let $C$ be the finite normal $A$-algebra of the pullback of $\mathcal N_\Omega$ to $\operatorname{Spec}A$; it is normal by localization of the normal model $N_T$. The field $\Omega$ is excellent and excellence passes to finite-type algebras and their localizations, so $A$ is excellent. The finite-algebra completion theorem identifies $D=R\otimes_A C$ with the finite product of the completed local rings $\widehat{C_{\mathfrak q}}$ for primes $\mathfrak q$ over the maximal ideal of $A$. Each $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal local domain by normality of $C$ and is excellent by the same finite-type/localization theorem. Fix such a $\mathfrak q$ and put $C'=C_{\mathfrak q}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. Being excellent, $C'$ is a G-ring by the definition of excellence, so the G-ring completion theorem (with $I=\mathfrak n$) makes $C'\to\widehat{C'}$ flat, with every fibre ring $\widehat{C'}\otimes_{C'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. Taking the trivial extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p')/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, which is finite purely inseparable by definition, each fibre ring is regular, hence normal by the regular-ring theorem. The completion $\widehat{C'}$ of the Noetherian ring $C'$ is Noetherian. The flat-normal-fibres theorem, applied to $C'\to\widehat{C'}$ with $C'$ Noetherian and normal, shows that $\widehat{C'}$ is normal (this is the argument of Tag 0C23). Finite products of normal rings are normal. Thus $D$ is normal. By compatibility of the maps it is the coordinate algebra of $\mathcal N_\Omega\times_{\mathcal X_\Omega}\operatorname{Spec}R$, and hence finite over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0DQZ (lemma-compare-versal-ring-completion); more-algebra.tex Tags 07QW, 07QU, 0C23 (lemma-completion-normal-local-ring); algebra.tex Tags 07N9, 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian) and 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian).

proof.text: The restriction of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ over $R^\circ$ is $E$, by step 4 and base change. It is schematically dense: before completion the open is dense in the normal chart model, and $A\to R$ is flat by the G-ring completion theorem, since excellence includes the G-ring property. The map $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is its base change and is flat. Flat pullback preserves this density. Hence the rational fields of all components of $E$ are exactly the total rational fields of $D$. Every element of $D$ is integral over $R$, and every element of that total rational algebra integral over $R$ is integral over $D$ and belongs to $D$, since $D$ is normal. This identifies $D$ canonically with the algebra $B$ of the statement. This is a calculation in the total rational algebra, not an assertion that integral closure commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 0C23 and algebra.tex Tag 07N9; affine normal integral-closure identification.

proof.text: Apply the finite-formal-quotient pullback theorem to $\mathcal N_\Omega\to\mathcal X_\Omega$. On the formal atlas its algebra is $D=B$ by steps 6--7, so its completion along the entire inverse image of the residual gerbe is $[\operatorname{Spf}B/H]$. The $H$-action used here is the action induced by the formal descent arrows, not an arbitrarily chosen lift. Under the integral-closure identification these arrows extend the given arrows on $E$: the algebra maps agree after restriction to the dense open, hence agree in the total rational algebra. The equivalence is therefore the claimed one over the specified formal chart.

source.place: Tags 04M9 and 044W on the infinitesimal neighbourhoods; Pikaart--de Jong Proposition 2.3.6, printed p.11, formal argument.

proof.text: For a closed point $b$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ over the closed point of $R$, its residue field is a finite extension of $\Omega$ and is therefore $\Omega$. In the quotient groupoid, an arrow from the object represented by this $\Omega$-point to itself is exactly an $h\in H$ with $h\cdot b=b$ as an $\Omega$-point; composition is multiplication in $H$. Since the action is $\Omega$-linear and the residue field is $\Omega$, fixing the closed point already fixes its $\Omega$-valued lift. The automorphism group is thus the stated stabilizer. If $B=0$ there is no such point, so this last assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Definition of the quotient groupoid and the stabilizer; cf. Tag 044R.
